read_rules.open: If no current reader, consume next part index before attempting open; open failure leaves current=None and consumed index.
read_rules.short_read: A positive response read returns immediately; it does not fill remaining caller buffer from the next part.
read_rules.eof: On Ok0 drop current reader before attempting next; skip empty parts; final EOF returns0 without time/account/publication.
read_rules.error: Read error propagates unchanged with current reader retained; no progress/time/publication. The outer downloader stops on error, without application retry.
read_rules.empty_buffer: No early empty-buffer return exists. Underlying readers returning0 cause all remaining parts to be opened/read/dropped, potentially draining the part list without bytes.

progress.initialization: 0e8dc9 samples now once; context done/rate/last_done=0, total from entire plan, reused across patch and optional EXE downloads.
progress.count: Response-reader bytes before payload gzip decode, not TCP/HTTP headers or decoded output. Add exact positive count with u64 wrapping; no total clamp.
progress.elapsed: 1456a1e60 samples now, subtracts last sample timestamp, saturates backwards to zero; convert seconds + nanos/1e9 to f64.
progress.threshold: elapsed>=0.25; below threshold retains old rate and previous sample byte/time lanes.
progress.rate: instantaneous=wrapping_sub(done,last_done) as f64 / elapsed; if old_rate==0 use instantaneous; otherwise 0.3*instantaneous+0.7*old_rate.
progress.reset: At a speed update call now a second time, store that timestamp and current done. Do not reuse elapsed's first timestamp.
